notes: Read SKILL.md (541 lines) in full; it is the only file. A dependency and supply-chain security guide for npm projects: npm audit/outdated, safe vs. forced fixes, monthly update routine, major framework upgrades on a branch, lockfiles and integrity, vetting new packages, typosquatting and dependency-confusion defenses (.npmrc scoped registries), Snyk, Dependabot, and CI audit gates.

Risk is medium because it has the agent install and update packages (`npm update`, `npm audit fix`, `npm install next@latest ...`, `npm install -g snyk`), commit lockfile changes and create branches (SKILL.md:107-223), authenticate Snyk with the user's account (`snyk auth`, `snyk monitor` sends the dependency graph to Snyk; SKILL.md:383-403), and add a CI workflow that uses a SNYK_TOKEN repository secret (SKILL.md:407-445). These are standard dependency-maintenance steps on the user's own project from official registries; `npm audit fix --force` is clearly flagged as risky with a test-before-commit procedure, so it is acceptable.

Self-contained: the `scripts/security-check.sh` it refers to (SKILL.md:52, 83, 522) is reproduced in full at SKILL.md:352-379, so the user can create it. The 'Current Status' section (SKILL.md:34-48: Next.js 15.5.4, 0 vulnerabilities) describes the Secure Vibe Coding OS starter at the time of writing, not the user's project. Minor inaccuracies: `npm audit fix` is described as never breaking (semver-minor updates can still break), and the CI example pins Node 18, which is end-of-life.
